platform_names: Payments [settings]; Payments [admin-navigation]; Payments > offline [settings]; Direct bank transfer [other:core-payment-gateways]; Check payments [other:core-payment-gateways]; Cash on delivery [other:core-payment-gateways]; PayPal Standard [other:core-payment-gateways]; Extensions > Official payments [other:marketplace-categories]; Payment Token API [term]; PCI-DSS compliance and WooCommerce [term]
plain_line: How a store takes buyers' payments through payment gateways: the core offline methods (direct bank transfer, check payments, cash on delivery), PayPal Standard, third-party payment extensions, saved payment methods, and the store's own PCI DSS compliance.
note: Joins the Payments settings tab and its core gateways with the Marketplace's Official payments category, saved payment tokens and the store's PCI-DSS compliance; no one menu of the platform's holds all of them.

platform_names: WooPayments [other:tos-woo-services]; Get paid with WooPayments [other:onboarding-tasks]; Account Management [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Payment Methods [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Compatibility [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Our Policies [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Know Your Customer [term]; built in partnership with Stripe [term]; Connected Account Agreement [legal-agreements]; PCI DSS [term]; payment token [term]; WooPay [term]
plain_line: Woo's own payment service: opening and verifying a WooPayments account, its payment methods, its partnership with Stripe and the licence under which funds are held and moved, its cardholder-data security, the saved-card tokens its payment partner holds, and WooPay's saved checkout details across stores.

platform_names: Fees and Debits [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Payouts [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Managing Money and Refunds [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; account balance [term]; reserve [term]
plain_line: The money side of WooPayments: its fees, the account balance and payouts, and reserves withheld for risk.
note: Joins WooPayments' own documentation topics Fees and Debits, Payouts, and Managing Money and Refunds with reserves. Merchant financing is in WC-A-29 (the review of the areas list, finding 3).

platform_names: Fraud and Disputes [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; fraud protection [term]; Stripe Radar [term]; Managing Disputes [term]; chargeback [term]
plain_line: Fraud screening and disputes on WooPayments transactions: the fraud protection rules the merchant sets, Stripe Radar's screening, and chargebacks.

platform_names: Currency [term]; base currency [term]; Currencies [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; multi-currency [term]; Payout currencies [term]; currency conversion fee [term]
plain_line: The store's one base currency, selling in more than one currency with WooPayments, and the currencies WooPayments pays out in, with its currency conversion fee.
note: Joins the store currency from the General settings tab with WooPayments' Currencies topic and its payout currencies, which the platform shows in different places.

platform_names: Selling location(s) [term]; Shipping location(s) [term]; Set up payments [other:onboarding-tasks]; payment-gateway-suggestions [term]; WooPayments in Your Country [term]; supported countries [term]; MaxMind Geolocation [other:core-integrations]; Default customer location [term]; Data [term]; data/countries [term]; data/continents [term]
plain_line: Where the store and Woo's services reach: the countries the store sells and ships to, the payment providers Woo suggests for each store country, the countries WooPayments serves, the country and continent data the store holds, and how the store locates a customer.
note: Brings together the platform's country lists and country settings, which sit in the General settings tab, the Payments suggestions, WooPayments' documentation and the data API; no menu of the platform's groups them.

platform_names: Restricted businesses and activities [legal-agreements]; Woo Guidelines for CBD and Other Hemp-Derived Products [legal-agreements]; Store guidelines [legal-agreements]; US Economic Sanctions [term]; OFAC [term]; export, import, and sanctions laws [term]
plain_line: Who may use Woo's services and what may be sold: businesses and activities restricted or prohibited on WooPayments, the guidelines for CBD and hemp-derived products, items prohibited in stores on WordPress.com sites, US sanctions on access to the services, and the export and sanctions laws that bind the merchant's own sales.
note: Joins three separate agreements and guidelines with the sanctions sections of the Terms of Service; together they say who may use what, which no menu shows.

platform_names: Terms of Service [legal-agreements]; Woo services [term]; WooCommerce, Inc. [term]; WooCommerce Ireland Ltd. [term]; Jurisdiction and Applicable Law [term]; Ecommerce Services [term]; Your responsibilities [term]; GPLv3 [legal-agreements]; open-source [term]; AI Guidelines [legal-agreements]; Artificial Intelligence [term]
plain_line: The agreements a merchant enters with Woo: which Woo company contracts, by whether the merchant resides in the Designated Countries, the governing law and courts, the merchant's own responsibility for the store's sales, receipts, refunds and consumer law, the open-source licence and warranty of the core software, and the AI Guidelines for Automattic's AI features.
note: Joins the Terms of Service with the GPLv3 licence and the AI Guidelines, three separate legal documents of the platform's.

platform_names: Privacy Policy [legal-agreements]; Privacy Notice for California Users [legal-agreements]; Do not sell or share my personal information [legal-agreements]; Controllers and Responsible Companies [term]; Transferring Information [term]; Request a data processing agreement [legal-agreements]; Data Processing Agreement [term]; Privacy considerations when using official payments extensions [term]; Privacy considerations when using official shipping extensions [term]
plain_line: How Automattic and Woo handle personal data: which company controls it, transfers outside the EEA and UK, Automattic as processor of site visitors' data under a data processing agreement, and the data shared with payment and shipping providers.
note: Joins the Privacy Policy and its related notices and agreement with the privacy pages for official payments and shipping extensions.

platform_names: WooCommerce usage tracking [legal-agreements]; wc-telemetry [term]; Remote Logging [other:features]; WooCommerce Analytics data syncing [legal-agreements]; Jetpack Sync [term]
plain_line: What the store sends to WooCommerce and Automattic: usage tracking, remote logging, WooCommerce Analytics data syncing and Jetpack Sync.
note: Joins two legal pages, a feature and the Jetpack terms, which all concern store data leaving the merchant's site for Woo or Automattic. The WordPress.com account and Jetpack connection are in WC-A-30 (the review of the areas list, finding 6).

platform_names: Tax [settings]; Collect sales tax [other:onboarding-tasks]; WooCommerce Tax [other:tos-woo-services]; Automated taxes [term]; Extensions > Store management > Sales tax and duties [other:marketplace-categories]; EU VAT Number [term]; customs charges, import taxes or duties [term]; VAT/GST/CT on fees [term]; Taxes and Documents [other:woopayments-doc-topics]; Form 1099-K [term]
plain_line: Taxes in and around the store: the tax rates the merchant enters, automated tax calculation by WooCommerce Tax, third-party tax extensions, EU VAT number collection, customs charges and import duties on shipments, taxes on Woo's own fees, and tax reporting tied to payments, such as Form 1099-K.
note: Joins the Tax settings tab with the WooCommerce Tax service, the Marketplace's Sales tax and duties category, the EU VAT Number extension, and the tax passages of the Terms of Service and WooPayments' documentation.

plain_line: Getting orders to customers: shipping zones, methods and classes, WooCommerce Shipping's labels and carrier rates, third-party carriers and shipping extensions, and order fulfillments.
note: Joins the Shipping settings tab with the WooCommerce Shipping service, the Marketplace's shipping category and the Order Fulfillments feature.

plain_line: The product catalogue: product types, variations, attributes, categories, tags and brands, inventory and stock, downloadable products and customer downloads, product reviews and review requests, CSV import and export, and cost of goods sold.
note: The Products menu and the Products settings tab, joined with the Cost of Goods Sold feature.

plain_line: Orders and their statuses, refunds, customers' order withdrawal requests, and the tables in which the store keeps its orders.
note: The Orders menu joined with refunds and two order features (Order withdrawal, High-Performance order storage).

plain_line: The buyer's cart and checkout: the cart and checkout pages, checkout rate limiting, address autocomplete, and shopper lists such as wishlists and save for later.
note: Joins several features and settings that all act on the cart and checkout; the platform has no one menu for them.

platform_names: WooCommerce > Customers [admin-navigation]; Accounts & Privacy [settings]; Personal data retention [term]; customer [access-scopes]; shop_manager [access-scopes]; manage_woocommerce [access-scopes]
plain_line: Customer accounts, the roles and capabilities of customers and shop managers, and the export, erasure and retention of customers' personal data.
note: Joins the Customers menu and the Accounts & Privacy settings tab with the store's roles and capabilities.

plain_line: Promoting the store: coupons and discounts, the Marketing hub's channels, campaigns and recommendations, order attribution, marketing extensions, MailPoet email marketing, and WooAds.
note: Joins the Marketing menu with the Order Attribution feature, the Marketplace's Marketing category, and two Woo services, MailPoet and WooAds.

platform_names: Emails [settings]; Emails > Email options [settings]; WooCommerce > Notifications [admin-navigation]; Back in Stock Notifications [other:features]
plain_line: The emails and notifications the store sends to the merchant and to customers about orders, accounts, refunds, fulfillments, reviews and withdrawals, and back-in-stock notifications.
note: Joins the Emails settings tab with the Notifications menu and the Back in Stock Notifications feature.

platform_names: Analytics [admin-navigation]; WooCommerce > Reports [admin-navigation]; WooCommerce Analytics [other:features]
plain_line: Analytics and reports kept in the store: revenue, orders, products, variations, categories, coupons, taxes, downloads and stock.

plain_line: Setting up and running the store from WooCommerce Home: the setup wizard, onboarding tasks and inbox, and whether the store shows as coming soon or is launched.
note: Joins the Home menu and Setup Wizard with the Site visibility settings tab.

platform_names: WooCommerce > Status [admin-navigation]; Status > Logs [admin-navigation]; Features [term]; Advanced > Blueprint (beta) [settings]; Own and control your store data – forever [other:plugin-page-features]; WooCommerce Server Recommendations [term]

note: Joins the Status menu with the Features settings, Blueprint, and the platform's statements on store data and hosting.

note: Joins the Advanced settings tab's API and Webhooks pages with the Store API, the Integration tab, block extensibility and the WooCommerce MCP feature.

plain_line: Finding, buying and installing extensions: the Woo Marketplace with its vendors' revenue share and refunds, Woo-made and third-party extensions and services, the connection to WooCommerce.com, and support for Woo and Marketplace products.

plain_line: How the storefront looks and reads: themes and block patterns, and extensions for cart and checkout features, product images and media, search and navigation, store page enhancements, and international and localization.
